title: KEC Wins INR 28.72 Billion in Indian Grid Orders
summary: 765 kV transmission projects linked to 8.5 GW of renewable generation highlight the infrastructure between generation and usable power.
body: What was announced

KEC International announced on 24 October that it had secured INR 2,872 crore — INR 28.72 billion — in turnkey orders from Power Grid Corporation of India. The scope covers design, supply, and installation of 765 kV transmission lines. According to KEC, the projects are associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat.
Why it matters for infrastructure

Generating capacity is not the same as electricity delivered where it is needed. Transmission provides the connection between new generation and wider demand. For data center site selection, this distinction matters: regional generation additions do not automatically establish available capacity at a particular substation.
What the announcement does not establish

These are contract awards, not completed lines or confirmed data center connections. The release does not establish the commissioning date, delivered output, project margin, or power availability for any individual compute campus.
Takeaway
Track network construction alongside generation. Before attaching a power premium to land, verify the relevant connection, delivery milestones, and contractual conditions.

title: Cardiff Shows Why On-Site Power Does Not Remove Planning Risk
summary: Community concerns around a proposed data center illustrate the permitting questions that remain when developers seek local generation.
body: The reported dispute

Local reporting and community material describe opposition to a proposed data center at Cardiff East Park and Ride. The debate includes a proposed temporary energy centre, environmental impacts, and the site's transport role. Published comment counts vary with the date and source; comments, objections, and petition signatures should not be treated as interchangeable.
The developer's position

In reporting by Herald.Wales, the developer said the scheme was designed to minimize environmental impacts while supporting economic investment. It also described proposed transport improvements. Those claims should be considered alongside the concerns raised by residents, not replaced by a one-sided description of the dispute.
What needs verification

A planning pause is not the same as a refusal, and a request for ministerial intervention is not proof that a project has been rejected. The latest decision status, generation design, operating conditions, and environmental assessments should be checked in the official planning record before investment decisions.
Takeaway

On-site generation may change the route to power, but it does not eliminate noise, air-quality, land-use, or community constraints. Time-to-Power analysis must include the approval path for the generation solution itself.
sources: Herald.Wales — local reporting and developer response
Save Cardiff East — community campaign, an interested party

title: Cable Capacity Is Another Constraint on Data Center Timelines
summary: Nexans' warning shifts attention from connection offers to the equipment required for energization.
body: The reported warning

Reuters reported on 22 October that Nexans' finance chief described cable manufacturing capacity as a constraint on AI data center construction. The report cited roughly three years to establish a new XLPE cable production line. That is a manufacturing expansion lead time, not a universal delivery time for every cable order.
Beyond the connection offer

Nexans also discusses this issue in its own industry commentary: a grid connection offer is not a commissioned electrical installation. Cable, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, testing, and installation must all align with the energization schedule. Supplier commentary is useful evidence of its perspective, not an independent forecast of every project's outcome.
What developers should check

Confirm specifications, production slots, delivery obligations, installation capacity, testing requirements, and interfaces between contractors. A procurement schedule should identify which components can actually determine the launch date.
Keep liability project-specific

Delay penalties and termination rights depend on signed contracts, caps, exclusions, and responsibility for the delay. There is no universal daily penalty that can be applied to all data center projects. The unsupported penalty examples in the original draft are not repeated here.
Takeaway
Time-to-Power includes the physical supply chain after the connection agreement. A credible schedule links utility milestones to equipment procurement, construction, and commissioning.
sources: Reuters via The Star — cable capacity report, 22 October 2026
Nexans — supplier commentary on electrical build-out
